subject_role: producer, mediator, channel, designed thing, or prior meaning in the cited design-historical account
target_role: consumer, audience, practice, or received meaning in that same account
output_state: a changed encounter, practice, or meaning
required_context: a named mediation channel and historical setting
required_qualification: which mediation sense and mediating actor are meant
scope_out: generic connection, legal mediation, or any-to-any bridging

subject_role: a work, movement, representation, or historical narrative selected for canonical status
target_role: a bounded design-historical canon or canonical status
input_state: contested historical material outside or unevenly positioned in a canon
output_state: greater canonical recognition or documented exclusion
required_context: an identified historiographic corpus and period
required_qualification: selection mechanisms and exclusions must be stated

subject_role: a named design occupation or disciplinary practice seeking professional standing
target_role: historically contested professional standing in a named field
input_state: a cited occupation or practice undergoing professional formation
output_state: a historically specific professional identity, status, or apparatus
required_context: named field, jurisdiction, period, and professional mechanisms
required_qualification: professional standing is historically contested and may exclude
scope_out: generic improvement, employment, or individual career advancement

subject_role: a named design logic, program, practice, or discipline carried by identified agents
target_role: a specified organization, field, or durable institutional arrangement
input_state: a cited practice or logic undergoing institutional embedding
output_state: a durable, legitimate, or reproduced institutional arrangement
required_context: named institution or field and identified carriers
scope_in: historical embedding and reproduction of design practices
scope_out: mere founding, popularity, or generic organizational presence

subject_role: actors, organizations, practices, ideas, or institutions crossing named national settings
target_role: other actors, organizations, practices, ideas, or institutions in those settings
input_state: separated but historically connected national settings
output_state: exchange, influence, friction, or network formation depending on the case
required_context: named parties, borders, institutions, and period
required_qualification: interaction mechanism and power relation must be explicit

subject_role: a cultural form, concept, practice, text, or translating agent in a named contact setting
target_role: a receiving cultural setting, interpretive community, or transformed form
input_state: a culturally situated form or meaning
output_state: an adapted, negotiated, or reconstituted meaning
required_context: named cultures, agents, medium, power relation, and period
required_qualification: transfer, adaptation, negotiation, and transformation senses must not be collapsed

subject_role: identified designers, institutions, exhibitions, or design communities participating in an exchange
target_role: the counterpart participants and situated design practices in that exchange
input_state: participants and practices brought into a named exchange
output_state: meetings, encounters, negotiations, or circulation outcomes
required_context: named participants, venue, political setting, and exchange mechanism
required_qualification: agency, reciprocity, and power asymmetry must be recorded

subject_role: a situated image, material, practice, history, or imaginative capacity made exchangeable
target_role: an exchangeable or market-valued commodity form
input_state: a situated cultural or material form not yet organized as the cited commodity
output_state: an exchangeable or market-valued commodity form
required_context: named market mechanism and historical setting
required_qualification: what becomes exchangeable and by whose action must be named
scope_out: all commercialization or consumption; decontextualization or branding without evidenced commodity status

subject_role: a design language, object, space, practice, role, or representation under analysis
target_role: a historically situated gender category, expectation, or subject position
output_state: a gender-coded meaning, use, role, or position
required_context: named design medium, audience, and gender regime
required_qualification: gender is performed and historically situated, not inherent in form
scope_out: essentialist claims that objects possess fixed gender

subject_role: people, practices, objects, images, energy systems, or meanings in a specified displacement account
target_role: a changed place, position, context, or condition
input_state: a situated prior place, context, or relation
output_state: forced movement, object relocation, conceptual reframing, or resistance depending on sense
required_context: named displaced entity, force, place, and period
required_qualification: forced, material, spatial, semantic, and strategic senses must be separated

subject_role: a cultural concept, practice, or knowledge system entering a contact process
target_role: locally negotiated cultural knowledge or practice
additional_party_roles: source communities; receiving communities; institutions; translators
input_state: contact among historically unequal cultural formations
output_state: multi-directional and continuing negotiation or reconstitution
required_context: named parties, locality, knowledge form, and period
scope_in: case-specific architectural and design knowledge circulation
scope_out: all cultural mixture, diffusion, or exchange

subject_role: people, forms, meanings, practices, or institutions moving in a specified cultural account
target_role: destinations, networks, or transformed contexts of that movement
input_state: a culturally situated actor or form
output_state: movement, contamination, exile, circulation, or transformed meaning depending on sense
required_context: named carrier, infrastructure, route, and period
required_qualification: material, human, semantic, and institutional mobility must be distinguished
scope_out: generic circulation or any cross-border change

subject_role: a designer, design community, institution, or national design discourse constructing its own cultural identity
additional_party_roles: external expectation, gaze, or anticipated audience
input_state: the actor's own cultural repertoire under external or internal expectations
output_state: a strategically selected self-representation emphasizing difference
required_context: named actor, audience, market, and cultural signs
required_qualification: agency, external gaze, and power asymmetry must remain explicit
scope_out: all use of tradition or any non-Western motif

subject_role: a historically constituted pattern of colonial power reproduced through design knowledge or practice
target_role: design institutions, methods, categories, or relations shaped by that pattern
additional_party_roles: institutions; knowledge systems; racialized and gendered subjects
output_state: reproduced hierarchies and normalized design forms
required_context: named colonial relation, design field, geography, and knowledge practice
required_qualification: coloniality is not interchangeable with colonialism or any inequality
scope_in: decolonial design analysis of enduring power patterns
scope_out: generic harm, all power, or a visual bridge node

subject_role: a maker, manufacturer, or design practice drawing from an identified prior design
target_role: the prior design, technique, form, or market example being imitated
input_state: an existing design or production example
output_state: a historically situated derivative design or production practice
required_context: named source, imitator, production regime, and period
required_qualification: imitation must not be equated automatically with infringement or piracy
scope_out: all influence, resemblance, appropriation, or inspiration

subject_role: an alleged copier, manufacturer, seller, or organized copying practice
target_role: a source or copied design, or a protected design interest
additional_party_roles: originator; rights claimant; regulator; court; trade body
input_state: a copying relation evaluated under a historical norm or legal-market regime
output_state: an allegation or historically situated classification of unauthorized copying
required_context: named jurisdiction, period, claimant, and protection regime
required_qualification: authorization, ownership claim, jurisdiction, legal or market status, ethical framework, and historical standard are mandatory
scope_out: generic resemblance, imitation, counterfeit, or moral condemnation
